lead: Electronic fuel injection (EFI) replaces the carburettor with a control loop. Sensors measure air flow, throttle angle, coolant temperature, exhaust oxygen and crank position. An electronic control unit (ECU) turns these signals into an injector pulse width. A fuel pump and pressure regulator keep fuel pressure fixed, so pulse width sets the fuel mass. EFI is used on almost every new petrol car, motorcycle and scooter in India because it holds the air-fuel ratio close to stoichiometric and cuts emissions.
prereq: You need: Chapter 2.2 for injection requirements and types, and Chapter 2.4 for the high-pressure rail idea behind direct injection.

blocks.text: The loop has five parts. Sensors turn physical quantities into electrical signals: a voltage, a change of resistance or a train of pulses. The ECU is a microprocessor with lookup tables and correction maps. Injectors are solenoid valves (some newer ones are piezo) that open when current flows. The fuel pump supplies more fuel than the engine needs. The pressure regulator returns the excess to the tank and holds delivery pressure constant, commonly about 3 bar for port injection. Because pressure is fixed, the ECU meters fuel only by changing injector open time, called pulse width.

items: Air flow sensor: hot-wire or hot-film type measures intake air mass; a manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor is used instead on speed-density systems.
Throttle position sensor (TPS): a potentiometer or Hall sensor reports idle, part load and wide-open throttle.
Coolant temperature sensor: a thermistor enriches the mixture when the engine is cold.

Crank position sensor: a magnetic or Hall pickup facing a toothed wheel on the crankshaft gives engine speed and piston position; a camshaft sensor tells the ECU which cylinder is on its compression stroke.
Oxygen sensor: a zirconia cell in the exhaust gives a voltage that switches either side of stoichiometric, about 14.7:1 by mass for petrol.

blocks.text: Open loop means the ECU uses tables only, with no oxygen feedback. It runs open loop during cold start, hard acceleration and wide-open throttle. Closed loop means the oxygen sensor trims the pulse width to hold the mixture near stoichiometric. The trim has a short-term correction and a long-term learned correction.

sections.h3: Mono-point: one injector at the throttle body

blocks.text: Mono-point EFI uses one injector mounted above the throttle plate in a throttle body. The injector sprays fuel into the incoming air, and the mixture travels through the intake manifold to all cylinders. Some syllabi call this single-point or throttle-body injection (TBI).

Fuel pressure is low, about 1 bar above manifold pressure, and the injector pulses in step with the crank signal, usually once for every cylinder firing, so each pulse serves whichever cylinder is drawing in. The ECU still uses the same sensors and oxygen feedback. Because fuel is delivered at one central point, cylinder-to-cylinder distribution depends on manifold geometry, so the mixture can be uneven. Wall wetting on a cold manifold also delays fuel response. Mono-point was a cheap retrofit for carburettors in the 1980s and 1990s. It is rare on new cars; multi-point and direct injection have replaced it.

Multi-point EFI (MPFI) has one injector per cylinder, mounted in the intake port just upstream of the inlet valve. Each injector sprays onto the back of the valve, so the fuel stays in the port and enters the cylinder as the valve opens. Port injection is another name. Fuel pressure is usually 3 to 4 bar.

Firing can be simultaneous, batch or sequential. In simultaneous firing all injectors open together once per revolution. In batch firing injectors are grouped, for example two groups that alternate. In sequential firing each injector opens just before its own cylinder's intake stroke. Sequential gives the best fuel control and cold-start behaviour, but it needs a camshaft sensor, because the crank sensor alone cannot tell the end of compression from the end of exhaust.

Compared with mono-point, MPFI gives better distribution, faster response and lower wall wetting. The intake manifold carries only air, so it can be tuned for air flow. The ECU can also cut fuel to one injector for a misfire or over-speed limit. MPFI is the common layout on Indian petrol cars and motorcycles. Petrol direct injection, with the injector inside the cylinder, is the next step; see Gasoline direct injection.

The ECU first estimates the air mass that enters one cylinder in one cycle, from the air-flow meter or from manifold pressure, speed and air temperature. It divides by the target A/F to get the fuel mass. Because the pressure across the injector is fixed, the injector passes a fixed static flow (g/s) while open, so the open time is the fuel mass divided by that flow. The needle takes a fraction of a millisecond to open, so the ECU adds a dead time that it raises when the battery voltage is low. Corrections for a cold engine, acceleration and oxygen-sensor trim then multiply the base pulse.

tinj = mair ÷ (A/F × qs) + tdead
mair is the air per cylinder per cycle (g); qs is the static injector flow (g/s); tdead is the opening delay (s).

examples.question: A port injector flows 240 cm³/min when fully open. The ECU holds it open for 5 ms. Find the fuel volume delivered in one injection in cm³ and mm³.
steps: Flow: 240 cm³/min ÷ 60 = 4 cm³/s; open time 5 ms = 0.005 s.
examples.answer: Fuel delivered per injection is 0.02 cm³, which is 20 mm³.
examples.check:
flow_cm3_per_min = 240
open_ms = 5
flow_cm3_per_s = flow_cm3_per_min / 60
open_s = open_ms / 1000
volume_cm3 = flow_cm3_per_s * open_s
volume_mm3 = volume_cm3 * 1000
print(volume_cm3)
print(volume_mm3)

examples.question: A four-cylinder MPFI engine runs at 3000 rpm and draws 0.35 g of air into each cylinder per cycle. The target is A/F = 14.7. Each injector flows 2.5 g/s of petrol when open and has a dead time of 0.8 ms. Find the pulse width and the fraction of the cycle the injector is open (sequential firing).
steps: Fuel per cylinder per cycle = 0.35 ÷ 14.7 = 0.02381 g.
Open time for that fuel = 0.02381 ÷ 2.5 = 0.009524 s = 9.52 ms.
One four-stroke cycle is 2 revolutions: at 3000 rpm that is 2 × 60 ÷ 3000 = 0.040 s = 40 ms.
examples.answer: Pulse width about 10.3 ms, open for about 26 % of each cycle. At 6000 rpm with the same air charge the cycle is 20 ms and the duty would be about 52 %.

traps: Mono-point does not mean one injector per cylinder. It means one injector in total, at the throttle body; multi-point has one per cylinder at the ports.
Pulse width sets fuel mass only because pressure is held constant. If the pressure regulator fails, the same pulse width gives a different fuel mass.
Closed loop needs a hot oxygen sensor. A cold engine runs open loop, so the ECU ignores the oxygen signal during warm-up.
Sequential injection needs cylinder identification from a camshaft sensor; batch and simultaneous firing can run from the crank sensor alone.
Forgetting the dead time. The pulse is the fuel time plus the opening delay; and one four-stroke cycle is two revolutions, not one.

quiz.q: What does the ECU change to meter fuel in a port injection system?
quiz.a: Pulse width, the injector open time, because fuel pressure is held constant.

quiz.q: Why does mono-point give poorer cylinder-to-cylinder fuel distribution than multi-point?
quiz.a: Mono-point delivers fuel at one central point, so manifold geometry and wall wetting affect how much fuel reaches each cylinder. Multi-point injects at each port, close to the valve.

quiz.q: An injector flows 180 cm³/min. It opens for 8 ms. Find fuel per injection in mm³.
quiz.a: 180 cm³/min = 3 cm³/s. Time = 0.008 s. Volume = 3 × 0.008 = 0.024 cm³ = 24 mm³.

quiz.q: The battery voltage of a car with EFI drops from 14 V to 11 V while it idles. Why does the ECU lengthen the pulse even though the fuel needed has not changed?
quiz.a: A lower voltage makes the injector coil current rise more slowly, so the needle opens later and the dead time grows. The fuel time is unchanged, so the ECU adds a longer dead time; without that the injector would deliver less fuel and the engine would run lean.

quiz.q: Name four sensors an EFI system reads.
quiz.a: Any four of: air-flow (or manifold pressure), throttle position, coolant temperature, crank position, camshaft position, oxygen sensor, intake air temperature.

quiz.q: What is the difference between open loop and closed loop?
quiz.a: Open loop uses stored tables and ignores the oxygen sensor. Closed loop uses the oxygen sensor to trim the pulse width toward stoichiometric.

quiz.q: An engine draws 0.30 g of air per cylinder per cycle at A/F 14.7. The injector flows 2.0 g/s and has 1.0 ms dead time. Find the pulse width.
A four-cylinder engine uses sequential injection. How many injector pulses occur per four-stroke cycle?
quiz.a: Four, one per cylinder per cycle.

beyond: Not for the exam. Wideband oxygen sensors give a continuous lambda reading instead of a switch, and model-based air-charge estimation replaces some sensors with software. Some engines combine port and direct injectors. Search for wideband lambda sensor, speed-density fuelling and injector dead-time calibration.
